title: Top-two economies protect their own supply
rule: The first and second-ranked economies at a port protect their supply from being netted out by other economies present there.
planner_implications: Keep must-have producer economies in the top two positions.

title: Top-two economies do not protect their demand
rule: Demand from the top two economies can still net against the supply of non-top-two economies.
planner_implications: Protected-supply status is not the same as full market immunity.

title: Two-economy mixes are the default safe design
rule: Two dominant economies can coexist without negative supply cannibalization, making two-economy mixes the default safe design recommendation.
planner_implications: Default to one or two dominant economies in high-confidence planner outputs unless a larger mix is deliberately justified.

title: Third-and-lower economies need pair-overlap review
rule: Once a third economy is present, Appendix D overlap details become mechanically relevant.
planner_implications: Do not greenlight a three-plus economy station without checking pair-overlap material.
testing_status: Supported by 35 extracted Appendix D entries

title: Contraband shaping is orbital-only
rule: Contraband strong links can only be created using orbital facilities.
planner_implications: Contraband plans must reserve orbital slots.

title: Insulating Membranes are orbital-only
rule: Insulating Membranes are restricted to orbital starports.
planner_implications: A pure-ground system cannot fully cover that material.
unknowns: Exact full product set of orbital-only materials

title: CMM Composites are planetary-only
rule: CMM Composites are restricted to planetary sites.
planner_implications: A pure-orbital system cannot fully cover that material.
unknowns: Exact full product set of surface-only materials

title: Refinery specialization requires the ground-only Refinery Hub
rule: Refinery markets can only be specialised directly through the ground-exclusive Refinery Hub.
planner_implications: Serious refinery systems need viable ground slots.

title: Development level affects commodity volume and seems to soft-cap near 20
rule: Development level affects commodity supply and demand volume and appears to soft-cap around level 20.
planner_implications: Development is a market-volume lever, not just decorative system flavor.
unknowns: Exact formula beyond the soft-cap observation

title: Steel is the dominant construction material
rule: Steel is required for all installations and often represents roughly 25-30% of total mass.
planner_implications: Steel coverage should be one of the first material checks in any construction-oriented planner.

title: CMM Composite, Aluminium, and Titanium are next-tier strategic materials
rule: CMM Composite, Aluminium, and Titanium are all called out as major construction materials with substantial share of facility mass requirements.
planner_implications: Material-completeness scoring should not stop at steel.

title: Planetary agriculture is mechanically valuable but reliability-limited
rule: Planetary agriculture can be a strong market source on paper, but bugged live behavior means some agricultural ports may produce no agri goods.
planner_implications: Prefer orbital agriculture when recommendation confidence matters more than slot purity.
unknowns: Which variants or systems are affected
